title: What It Actually Costs to Build Your Own Canvassing Team
content:
###  **The Hourly Wage Is Only the Start** 

When a company decides to build its own canvassing or field team, the conversation usually starts and ends with an hourly wage. That number is the smallest part of the actual cost. 

###  **What Gets Left Out of the Math** 

Recruiting takes time. Training takes time and does not guarantee the person stays past their first paycheck. Someone has to manage the team day to day, which is rarely free — it is either a manager's salary or a business owner's own hours pulled away from running the company. 

###  **The Turnover Problem** 

Field roles have some of the highest turnover of almost any position. A company that hires four people to keep two in the field over a season is paying for six onboarding cycles to get two consistent workers. 

###  **A Different Way to Think About It** 

Before committing to building a team from the ground up, it is worth understanding what a structured alternative actually costs in comparison — often less than expected once the full picture is accounted for.
